simple.meaning: מַפָּלָה (mappâlâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “something fallen , i.e. a ruin.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: מַפָּלָה (H4654) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Isaiah 17:1, with occurrences in Isaiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַפָּלָה (H4654) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in מַפָּלָה (H4654) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: מַפָּלָה (mappâlâh) / H4654 is traced through Isaiah 17:1, Isaiah 23:13, Isaiah 25:2 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

majorEvents.evidenceText: Behold, the land of the Chaldeans. This people didn’t exist. The Assyrians founded it for those who dwell in the wilderness. They set up their towers. They overthrew its palaces. They made it a ruin.
